chunks: ʿUmar, the companion of al-Karābīs, narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

Concerning a man who made a mukātabah contract with his slave and stipulated against him that his inheritance would belong to him; that was then brought before ʿAlī عليه السلام, so he invalidated his condition and said:
The condition of Allah precedes your condition.

key_terms.شَرْطُ اللَّهِ: the divinely established condition or ruling
key_terms.شَرْطِكَ: your personal stipulation or contractual condition
key_terms.كَاتَبَ: entered into a contract of manumission with a slave

ai.seo_question: Can a master stipulate in a mukātabah contract that the slave’s inheritance returns to him?
ai.summary: This hadith states that a stipulation in a mukātabah contract giving the master the slave's inheritance is invalid. Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام ruled that divine law takes precedence over private contractual conditions, establishing a principle in jurisprudence that unlawful conditions are void.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3490 - Umar, the companion of al-Karabis, narrated from Abu Abdullah (as), regarding a man who entered into a mukataba (a contract of emancipation) with his slave and stipulated that the slave's inheritance would belong to him (the master).
This case was presented to Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) , who invalidated the condition and said:
"The condition of Allah (swt) precedes your condition."
